How to Deploy an AI-Built Startup Without Burning Cash on Hosting

AI tools let anyone build a working app in hours. But hosting costs can eat your runway before you get your first customer. Here's how to deploy on your own server for a fraction of the price.

The AI Startup Boom

Something fundamental changed in 2025–2026. Tools like Cursor, v0, Bolt, Claude, and ChatGPT made it possible for anyone - not just engineers - to build a working product in a weekend. You describe what you want, the AI writes the code, and suddenly you have a SaaS, a marketplace, an internal tool, or a mobile backend that actually works.

This is great news for founders. The cost of building software dropped to nearly zero. But the cost of running software didn't.

The Hosting Cost Trap

Here's the problem most AI-built startups hit: the app works on your laptop, but to put it in front of real users you need a server. And the "easy" hosting options are expensive.

Let's look at the typical monthly cost for a small startup running a web app, a database, Redis, and a few background workers:

Platform Monthly Cost What You Get
Vercel / Netlify $20–$250+ Frontend only, no database
Railway / Render $50–$300+ Full-stack, but usage-based pricing spikes fast
Heroku $100–$500+ Easy but expensive at scale
AWS / GCP (managed) $100–$500+ Powerful but complex, requires DevOps knowledge
Your own server + Stacker $5–$20 Full control, everything included
The math is simple. A $5–$20/month VPS (Hetzner, DigitalOcean, Contabo) can run a production web app, PostgreSQL, Redis, a reverse proxy with SSL, and background workers. That's 10–50x cheaper than managed platforms.

Why Stacker?

The problem with self-hosting has always been the operational overhead. You need to know Docker, networking, SSL certificates, reverse proxies, database backups, firewall rules… It's a full-time job.

Stacker removes that overhead. It's a single CLI tool that takes your project - the one AI generated for you - and deploys it to your own server in a few commands. No YAML file hell, no Kubernetes, no manual nginx configuration.

Step-by-Step: Deploy Your AI-Built App

Let's say you built a SaaS with Next.js (frontend), PostgreSQL (database), and Redis (caching) using Cursor or ChatGPT. Here's how to get it live on your own server.

1. Get a Cheap Server

Rent a VPS from any provider. Hetzner is the best value in Europe (CX22: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 40 GB disk for ~€5/month). DigitalOcean and Vultr are good alternatives. You need roughly 2–4 GB of RAM for most small apps.

2. Add a stacker.yml to Your Project

This is the only file you add. It tells Stacker what your app is, what services it needs, and where to deploy: 

# stacker.yml
name: my-startup
app:
  type: node
  ports:
    - "3000:3000"
  environment:
    NODE_ENV: production

services:
  - name: postgres
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: pg_isready -U postgres

  - name: redis
    image: redis:7-alpine
    command: redis-server --requirepass ${REDIS_PASSWORD}

volumes:
  pgdata: {}

deploy:
  target: server
  server:
    host: 123.45.67.89
    user: root
    ssh_key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519

proxy:
  type: nginx
  domains:
    - domain: myapp.com
      ssl: auto
      upstream: app:3000

3. Deploy

One command: 

stacker deploy

That's it. Stacker will:

  • Detect your project type and generate a Dockerfile
  • Build a Docker Compose stack from your stacker.yml
  • Copy everything to your server over SSH
  • Start all containers (app, database, Redis)
  • Configure nginx with automatic SSL (Let's Encrypt)
  • Set up firewall rules to open only the ports you need

Your app is now live at myapp.com.

What If You Need More Services?

Most real apps need more than just a web server and a database. Maybe you want analytics, a queue, file storage, or monitoring. Stacker handles multi-service stacks natively: 

services:
  - name: postgres
    image: postgres:16-alpine
  - name: redis
    image: redis:7-alpine
  - name: rabbitmq
    image: rabbitmq:3-management
  - name: minio
    image: minio/minio
    command: server /data
  - name: worker
    image: myapp/worker:latest
    command: python worker.py

All services run in isolated containers on the same Docker network. They can talk to each other by service name (postgres, redis, rabbitmq) - no IP addresses, no manual networking.

The Cost Comparison: Real Numbers

Let's compare a realistic startup setup over 12 months:

Setup Monthly Yearly
Railway (web + DB + Redis + worker) ~$150 ~$1,800
Vercel + PlanetScale + Upstash ~$80 ~$960
Heroku (dyno + Postgres + Redis) ~$250 ~$3,000
Hetzner VPS + Stacker ~$8 ~$96
That's $800–$2,900 saved per year. For a bootstrapped startup, that's real runway - months of server costs covered by the savings alone.

Common Concerns

"What about uptime?"

A Hetzner CX22 has a 99.9% uptime SLA. For most startups, that's better than you need. If you outgrow one server, Stacker supports multi-server deployments too. And you can always set up a simple status page to monitor your services.

"What about backups?"

Stacker uses named Docker volumes for persistent data. You can back up your database with a simple cron job, or use stacker agent to manage remote operations. Don't rely on your hosting provider's backups as your only safety net - a 5-minute pg_dump cron job is enough for most startups.

"What about security?"

Stacker handles SSL automatically (Let's Encrypt). It also configures firewall rules so only necessary ports are open. The stacker.yml format supports config_contract to declare which fields are secrets - Stacker generates strong values automatically and stores them securely.

"I don't know Docker. Is this still for me?"

Yes. Stacker auto-detects your project type (Node, Python, Rust, Go, PHP, or static) and generates the Docker configuration for you. You never write a Dockerfile. The stacker.yml above is the entire configuration.

What About AI-Generated Projects Specifically?

AI tools produce projects that follow standard conventions: package.json for Node, requirements.txt for Python, Cargo.toml for Rust. Stacker's auto-detection works perfectly with these. The same tools that generated your app in hours now deploy it in seconds.

The workflow looks like this:

  1. Build with Cursor / v0 / Claude / ChatGPT (hours, not weeks)
  2. Test locally on your laptop
  3. Deploy with stacker deploy (seconds, not days)
  4. Iterate - push changes with stacker deploy again

Total infrastructure cost: under $10/month. Total time spent on operations: minutes.

Getting Started

Ready to try it? Here's what you need:

  • A server - any VPS with 2+ GB RAM (~$5/month on Hetzner)
  • Stacker - install with one command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/trydirect/stacker/main/install.sh | bash
  • Your project - the one you already built with AI

Then add your stacker.yml, run stacker deploy, and you're live.

The Bottom Line

AI lowered the cost of building software to near zero. Stacker lowers the cost of running it to near zero. Together, they let a solo founder or small team build and ship a real product for less than the price of a coffee subscription.

The next time an AI tool gives you a working app in a weekend, don't pay $200/month to put it online. Get a $5 server, add a stacker.yml, and deploy.
